Dashboard & Reports: Functional integration tests for aggregate/read-only dashboard and reporting endpoints across AdminController
An admin views platform-wide dashboard statistics, including a 7-day registration trend and the top courses by enrollment.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR in an environment with existing users/courses/enrollments.
2. Prepare GET /api/admin/dashboard/stats with the Authorization header set.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response's totalUsers/totalCourses/totalEnrollments, the 7-day weeklyLabels[]/weeklyValues[] trend, and topCourses[].
column4: 1. 200 OK; totalUsers, totalRoles, totalCourses, totalEnrollments, weeklyLabels[]/weeklyValues[] (7 entries, oldest-to-newest, real registration counts per day), topCourses[] (up to 5, by enrollment count).

column3:
1. As any logged-in role, trigger a few real AI calls beforehand (e.g. AI Assistant messages, AI question generation).
2. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR and prepare GET /api/admin/ai-usage.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response's totalCalls/successCount/failureCount/chatCalls/embeddingCalls/successRate and the 7-day weekly trend.

column5: - ADMINISTRATOR logged in; ≥1 real AI call logged beforehand.

Dashboard & Reports: A trainer's dashboard correctly aggregates their own courses, learners, exams, revenue, and rating into a single summary.
column3:
1. Log in as a trainer who owns at least one course with some enrolled learners and payments.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/dashboard.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect coursesCount, learnersCount, examsCount, totalRevenue, averageRating, courses[], and monthlyRevenues[] in the response.
column4: 1. 200 OK; coursesCount, learnersCount (distinct across all the trainer's courses), examsCount, totalRevenue (defaults to 0, never null), averageRating, courses[] (one row per course family, most-recent version, with versionsCount), monthlyRevenues[] (12 fixed Jan-Dec entries for the current year, zero-filled where no revenue).
column5: - Logged in as an eligible authoring role; owns ≥1 course with some learners/payments.

Dashboard & Reports: The trainer dashboard's \recent activities\" feed correctly merges three different event types by recency and caps the combined list at 5 entries."
column3:
1. Ensure the trainer has more than 5 combined recent payment, enrollment, and rating events across their courses.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/dashboard.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect recentActivities[] — count the entries and check the relative-time strings.
column4: 1. recentActivities[] contains at most 5 entries total, drawn from the union of the last 5 payments + last 5 enrollments + last 5 ratings, re-sorted and capped to the 5 most recent overall, each with a human-readable relative "time" string ("X mins/hours/days ago").
column5: - ≥6 combined recent payment/enrollment/rating events exist for the trainer's courses.

Dashboard & Reports: The inactiveCoursesCount figure silently undercounts submitted-for-review courses, because it queries the literal status string \PENDING\" instead of the real \"PENDING_APPROVAL\" value that submission actually sets (confirmed likely bug
column4:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and note the current inactiveCoursesCount via GET /api/v1/course-manager/dashboard.
2. As a trainer, submit a DRAFT course for review so its status becomes PENDING_APPROVAL.
3. As COURSE_MANAGER, call GET /api/v1/course-manager/dashboard again.
4. Compare the before/after inactiveCoursesCount values.
column5: 1. inactiveCoursesCount does NOT increase after the submission — the course sitting in PENDING_APPROVAL is silently excluded from the count, since no course is ever persisted with the literal status "PENDING" that the query actually filters on.
column6: - COURSE_MANAGER logged in; a DRAFT course ready to submit.

Dashboard & Reports: A plain TRAINER account is forbidden from viewing the Course-Manager dashboard, even though the URL itself is public at the filter level.
column3:
1. Log in as a plain TRAINER account (no COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR role).
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/course-manager/dashboard with that account's Authorization header.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status, confirming the request does reach the controller before being denied by method security.
column4: 1. 403 Forbidden — confirm this is actually enforced given the URL-level permitAll (i.e. the request does reach the controller before being denied by method security).

Dashboard & Reports: A trainer's own course-list view bundles status-count badges computed from their FULL course set, independent of whatever narrow status/search filter is currently applied to the visible list.
column3:
1. Log in as a trainer with courses across at least 3 different statuses.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/trainer/courses?status=DRAFT&search=xyz (a narrow filter expected to match few or zero courses).
3. Send the request.
4. Compare the returned courses[] (should be narrowly filtered) against the count badges (allCount/draftCount/publishedCount/hiddenCount/pendingCount/rejectedCount) in the same response.
column4: 1. The count badges reflect the trainer's FULL, unfiltered course set — they do not shrink to match the narrow status=DRAFT&search=xyz filter, while courses[] itself IS correctly filtered.
column5: - Trainer with courses across ≥3 different statuses.
